steps.title: Capture and save a screenshot
actions: Press Windows logo key + Shift + S, then select the area to capture.
Open the capture in Snipping Tool. Select Save as and choose Downloads as the location.
steps.done: Attach it only to the helpdesk request that asked for it. Check the image for names or other private details first.

source.title: Use Snipping Tool to capture screenshots

steps.title: Capture and save a screenshot
actions: Press Shift-Command-5 to open Screenshot.
Open Options and choose Downloads as the save location. Choose a capture or recording mode and start it.
steps.done: Attach it only to the helpdesk request that asked for it. Check the image for names or other private details first.

steps.title: Find your connection information
actions: Connect to your remote session in Windows App.
On the connection toolbar, select the signal-strength icon to open Connection Information.
Select Details and read the Transport protocol, Round-trip time, and Available bandwidth lines. They describe this session, not the browser check.
steps.whatYouShouldSee: The transport protocol (UDP or WebSocket) and round-trip time used by this remote session.
steps.done: Share the values with your helpdesk if they asked for them.

source.title: Configure RDP Shortpath: verify the transport

steps.title: Collect Windows App diagnostic logs on Windows
actions: Open Windows App on your Windows device and select Settings (the gear icon) or About.
Select Export diagnostic logs (or Open logs folder) and save the archive to your Downloads folder.
steps.whatYouShouldSee: A diagnostic log folder or zip file in Downloads.
steps.done: Send the logs only through the support channel your helpdesk named. Never attach diagnostic logs to a public GitHub issue.

steps.title: Collect Windows App diagnostic logs on macOS
actions: In Windows App on your Mac, open the Help menu in the menu bar and select Troubleshooting.
Select Export diagnostic logs and choose Downloads as the destination.
steps.whatYouShouldSee: A Windows App diagnostic log archive in Downloads.
steps.done: Send the archive only through the support channel your helpdesk named.

steps.title: Collect Windows App diagnostic logs on iPad or iPhone
actions: Open Windows App on your iPad or iPhone and tap Settings.
Tap Troubleshooting, then tap Share diagnostic logs and save the file to Files (Downloads).
steps.whatYouShouldSee: The diagnostic log archive saved in the Files app.
steps.done: Share the file only through your organization's approved helpdesk channel.

steps.title: Collect Windows App diagnostic logs on Android
actions: Open Windows App on your Android device and tap Settings.
Tap Troubleshooting, then tap Share diagnostic logs and save the file to Downloads.
steps.whatYouShouldSee: The diagnostic log archive in Downloads.
steps.done: Share the file only through your organization's approved helpdesk channel.

steps.title: Collect Windows App web client diagnostic logs
actions: In the browser tab running windows.cloud.microsoft, select Settings (the gear icon) in the top bar.
Open About or Troubleshooting and select Download diagnostic logs to save the log file to Downloads.
steps.whatYouShouldSee: A web client log file in Downloads.
steps.done: Send the file only through the support channel your helpdesk named.

steps.title: Collect Teams support logs
actions: In Teams inside the remote session, press Ctrl + Alt + Shift + 1.
Wait for the Downloading web logs banner to go away, then look in that session's Downloads folder.
steps.whatYouShouldSee: A Teams support log file in Downloads.
steps.done: Send the file only through the channel your helpdesk named. Logs can contain private diagnostic information.

source.title: Collect log files for monitoring and troubleshooting in Teams

steps.title: Collect Teams support logs
actions: In Teams, open the Help menu and select Collect support files, or press Option + Command + Shift + 1.
Wait for the Downloading web logs banner to go away, then look in Downloads.
steps.whatYouShouldSee: A Teams support log file in Downloads.
steps.done: Send the file only through the channel your helpdesk named. Logs can contain private diagnostic information.

source.title: Collect log files for monitoring and troubleshooting in Teams

steps.title: Run the Microsoft Shortpath test
actions: Open Microsoft's RDP Shortpath guide and find Check client device STUN/TURN server connectivity and NAT type.
Download and run avdnettest.exe on your own device only if your helpdesk asks you to. This page does not download or run it.
steps.whatYouShouldSee: The test's local output in its window.
steps.done: Give the output to your helpdesk through its approved support channel. Do not attach it to a public issue.

source.title: Configure RDP Shortpath: check client device connectivity

steps.title: Collect Multimedia Redirection (MMR) logs
actions: Inside the remote browser where video playback is redirected, open the Azure Virtual Desktop Multimedia Redirection extension popup.
Select Collect logs (or Export logs) and save the log file to Downloads.
steps.whatYouShouldSee: An MMR diagnostic log file in Downloads.
steps.done: Send the file only through your helpdesk's approved support channel.

source.title: Troubleshoot Multimedia Redirection for Azure Virtual Desktop

steps.title: Prepare files for the signed log bundle collector
actions: Download avd-linecheck-result.json (and optional comments.txt or captures) from the network check into your Downloads folder.
If your administrator gave you the signed avd-current-state client log collector script, run it on your device so it packages your result and client logs into one archive.
steps.whatYouShouldSee: Your saved result files in Downloads ready for the collector script.
steps.done: Review the resulting bundle before sending it to your helpdesk through its approved support channel.
